core.description: Core — a KeysProvider hears every key on the page, keeps the Keys, and calls every Enabled useKeys; it Takes the keys of the Bindings declared in it and refuses those that Conflict. Bindings are written with shortcut() and sequence().

key names one Key; binding writes Shortcuts and Sequences and says when two Conflict; key-input listens to the page and keeps the Kept Keys from it; keymap matches keys to declared Bindings; provider puts them together for React.

recognizers.description: Recognizers — the hooks an app calls: useShortcut and useSequence, each declaring its Bindings to the nearest KeysProvider. They never know about each other.
Each Recognizer declares its keys through the provider on its own.

surfaces.description: Surfaces — an app's whole keyboard from one central definition: its Surfaces and Actions, the Active Surface the app names, and the Handlers it gives. It declares only the Bindings that work to the core.
surface-tree reads the definition and says which Bindings work for an Active Surface, without React; create-keys gives the Provider and the typed hooks.

use-keys.description: Recognizers and Surfaces are built on the core and never know each other; the core never imports them. Each layer is its own entry point.
